scope: Source-scope review only; full-model execution and publication remain separate requirements.

source_stage_review.realization: Prepare decoded RGB/binary raster pairs using source unshifted and half-shifted grids, mask-area ordering, JPEG roundtrip and selected tile populations.
source_stage_review.correction: Raster decoding is a caller boundary. Grid padding, source ordering and lossy preprocessing remain explicit; no arbitrary interchangeable tiler is claimed.

source_stage_review.realization: Use source RGB/BGR conversion, JPEG preprocessing and fixed channel normalization in augmentation and inference.
source_stage_review.correction: The intake stain-normalization claim is unsupported by the qualified source. Do not represent fixed channel normalization as stain normalization. This correction must be explicit in the corrected graph.

source_stage_review.realization: Use full SE-ResNeXt101 encoder with custom decoder, attention and hypercolumns; execute initial folds, model restoration, generated pseudo masks and fresh retraining folds.
source_stage_review.correction: Replace the intake DeepLabV3+/ResNeSt50 description with the source architecture. Initial training and pseudo-label retraining are required lifecycle stages omitted by the intake. Explicit encoder states are required; no automatic pretrained download.

source_stage_review.realization: Train with binary BCE and per-image Lovasz hinge plus four nonempty-only deep supervision terms weighted0.1 and image-classification BCE.
source_stage_review.correction: This is binary Lovasz hinge, not multiclass Lovasz-Softmax. Preserve auxiliary losses and their empty-mask gradient behavior.

source_stage_review.realization: Use four flip views for pseudo labels and three for final prediction; average models and views before resize and strict binary thresholding.
source_stage_review.correction: Pseudo and final inference policies differ. Batch-wide classification shortcut and ensemble order remain source assumptions; binary masks are not calibrated probabilities.

source_stage_review.realization: Prepare padded inference grids in bounded batches and write predicted interiors into a full-size binary output mask.
source_stage_review.correction: Full decoded source and output arrays remain resident. No TIFF streaming, unbounded-size memory guarantee or source-codec qualification is implied.

reuse_decision: The recipe may transfer to other binary raster-segmentation tasks with justified foreground semantics, physical scale, color and augmentation assumptions, independent grouped populations and pseudo-source isolation. Keep explicit stage and inference policies. Generic image or sampling operations require independent qualification before standalone selection.
limitations: Binary foreground semantics, physical scale, color statistics and lossy preprocessing must be justified for each application. A nonempty mask can enter the background sampling population. TIFF decoding and stain normalization are not implemented by this graph.

Group labels do not establish independence of subjects, acquisition sessions or sources. The caller must exclude validation overlap from pseudo sources; the implementation does not detect that overlap.

Encoder-state shape compatibility and deterministic seeds do not authenticate pretrained weights or prove accuracy. Explicit stage schedules and checkpoint roles must be executable. The graph stage functions use _train_stages directly and do not inherit all run_lifecycle selector validation.

Pseudo masks are model outputs, not independent ground truth. Positive-only filtering, area bins and augmentation invariance are recipe assumptions; application transfer requires justification and independent evaluation.

Batch composition, tile scale, padding, normalization and thresholds affect meaning and output. An empty final mask can result from the classifier shortcut; it is not evidence of absent foreground. Binary outputs are not calibrated uncertainty estimates.

These provider interfaces are recipe stages and trusted runtime-object boundaries, not a generic JSON service. Image tiling, balanced sampling and aggregation need independently qualified contracts before standalone cross-domain selection.
remaining: Execute full initial and retraining networks, pseudo handoff and final prediction with explicit fold coverage, source-sized geometry and bounded resources.
Review provider contracts and reconcile metadata with rollback gates.
Stage and execute the corrected stored original; qualify publication and served selection.
